submitter: leopardess3 / cta_link_integrity workstream (round 3 — implements the round-2 arbitration; round 1 voided by bugs_open/019, round 2 REJECTED with direction)
rationale:
BE CONCISE. A reviewer whose output hits the token cap voids the ENTIRE round and discards every other seat's work (bugs_open/019 — it killed round 1 of this trail). Name your decision and your single strongest objection; one or two sentences per point; do not restate the plan.

This round is not a re-argument. Round 2's near-unanimous direction was: ship Option A (a scoped migration) now as the safe stopgap, land Option B's consolidation with the plan_sections edit STAGED observe-only, then retire A's pattern. This plan implements exactly that, and fixes the four defects the seats named:

1. (bug_historian medium, debug_historian high) I had staged the low-risk edit and shipped the high-risk one live. FIXED: plan_sections is now observe-only in this round — it logs would-be ownership conflicts and changes nothing. The write flips only in a follow-up submission after one real build's delta log is read.
2. (guidelines medium) My skip branch did a bare continue when fallback was nil, leaving a required:true field unset — the forbidden empty default. FIXED in the flip design (documented in edit 5's sketch): the eventual skip honours on_missing/required; it never silently drops a required field.
3. (bug_historian medium) The sibling-label rule relocated the map's silent failure mode. FIXED: edit 2 adds UncoveredCTAURLFields — a loud-fail guard that surfaces every *_url field with a query-resolved source and NO sibling label, logged at build time, so an uncovered CTA is visible instead of silently overwrite-prone.
4. (debug_historian medium) No deploy verification. FIXED: risks now specify pod-binary verification by grepping the running pod for the distinctive log string, per the repo's standing rule — never inferred from tag or commit.

Also applied: guardian's recommendation to unbundle the applyCTARecompute widening — it is DROPPED from this round and ships independently after the delta logs are reviewed. And editquality's Q4 caveat ('A isn't as mechanical as advertised') sharpened the migration's scope: it flips ONLY the site_specs.cta.* fields on components already inside ctaFieldNames — the /contact.html-lock fossil class, where the resolver genuinely writes and genuinely loses. Nav/legal/contact url fields sourced from site_specs are legitimately site-config-owned and are NOT touched; flipping a field the resolver does not write would orphan it.

Remaining open question for reviewers: is the observe-only conflict log in plan_sections (edit 5) acceptable in the hot path? It is one map lookup and a conditional Info log per CTA field — no queries, no writes.

plan.summary: Round-2 direction implemented: (A) a scoped, live-immediately migration flips the /contact.html-fossil CTA url fields (site_specs.cta.* on ctaFieldNames components) to source 'renderer', closing the known overwrite defect with zero Go; (B) the schema-derived CTA pairing lands as a shared helper with a loud-fail guard for unconventional fields, wired OBSERVE-ONLY into both resolve_internal_links and plan_sections — logs only, no behaviour change anywhere in Go this round. The write-path flip and the applyCTARecompute widening are explicit follow-ups, each gated on reading one real build's delta logs.

edits.rationale: Option A, scoped per the council's own caveat: flip source to 'renderer' ONLY for CTA url fields that (a) sit on a component whose function is in ctaFieldNames AND (b) currently carry a site_specs.cta.* source. These are the fields the resolver writes today and loses to re-resolution — the 143-of-144-buttons-to-/contact.html fossil (live example: header-bold-gradient cta_url source pages.contact, found by diagnosis c84940fb). Fields the resolver does NOT write (nav/legal/contact site_specs sources) are untouched — flipping them would orphan the value. Config-only, live immediately, no image roll.

edits.rationale: One definition of 'this field is a button destination' (same consolidation motive as links.go), PLUS the loud-fail guard the council required: unconventionally-named url fields must surface, not silently fall out of coverage.

Pins the exclusion case (guide_image_url/logo_url must NOT derive), the _text suffix, nil-schema safety, deterministic ordering, and the loud-fail guard (a site_specs-sourced url with no label IS returned by UncoveredCTAURLFields; a site_assets image url is NOT).
edits.sketch:
schema := fields{cta_primary_url:{source: site_specs.cta.primary_url},
  cta_primary_label:{source: static}, guide_image_url:{source: site_assets.image},
  orphan_cta_url:{source: site_specs.cta.secondary_url}}
Derive -> exactly [cta_primary_url paired with cta_primary_label]
Uncovered -> exactly [orphan_cta_url]   // not guide_image_url
+ nil/empty schema -> nil, no panic; ordering deterministic.

edits.rationale: Observe-only, unchanged in intent from round 2 (no seat objected to this edit's staging): log the derived-vs-map delta per component, plus one Warn per UncoveredCTAURLFields hit. ctaFieldNames still decides every write this round; its doc comment gains 'now an override for non-conforming components; stage-2 inverts precedence after delta review'.

THE PREVIOUSLY-CONTESTED EDIT, now staged exactly as the council required: this round it only LOGS. For each derived CTA field on the section, if query re-resolution is about to write a value that DIFFERS from one already present in resolved_data, log the would-be overwrite. No skip, no write change, no new queries (it reads what the loop already resolved). The follow-up flip — a separate submission after one real build's log is read — will skip re-resolution for resolver-owned fields, and its skip branch honours on_missing/required (guidelines' objection): a required field with no fallback defers per the schema's own on_missing, never a bare continue.

grounded_in: Round-2 council verdict (trail 2525f980): guardian veto notes 'ship Option A now; keep edits 1, 2 (observe-only) and 4 as prep, drop edit 3 pending architecture review'; guidelines 'ship A now as the safety valve, land B behind the observe-only stage, then retire A's pattern'; debug_historian 'justified only if staged like the resolve_internal_links edit'.

guidelines objection (round 2): 'when ctaOwnedURLFields[fieldName] is true and fallback is nil, the field is left unset (bare continue) — if required:true this is exactly the skip_field/empty default the rule forbids'.

bug_historian objection (round 2): 'a component whose CTA url field doesn't follow the convention silently falls out of derivation with no warning — the map's exact failure mode relocated … proposes no loud-fail guard (e.g. logging *_url fields with no sibling and a query-resolved source)'.

Diagnosis c84940fb (CONFIRMED): query-resolved sources (site_specs.*, pages.*, site_assets.*, config.*) re-run their lookups on every plan_sections call and overwrite resolver output; live fossil: header-bold-gradient cta_url {source: pages.contact, fallback: /contact.html}.

Live library 2026-07-19: derived rule = 119 CTA url fields / 33 functions; ctaFieldNames covers 5 of 33 functions; 83 fields query-resolved, of which the site_specs.cta.* class on mapped components is the subset the resolver both writes and loses — the migration's exact target.
plan.risks:
1. Migration scope: flipping a field the resolver does not write would orphan it — scoped to ctaFieldNames components + site_specs.cta.* sources only, snapshot first, ledger row in the same transaction (007). Reviewer check: confirm the WHERE clause cannot touch nav/legal/contact fields.
2. Hot-path cost of the plan_sections observe log: one map lookup + conditional Info per CTA field, no queries. If any seat judges even that unacceptable, say so — it can move behind a config flag.
3. Deploy verification (Go edits are inert until an image roll): after rollout, verify against the RUNNING POD, never the tag — `kubectl exec <pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c "cta derivation delta"'` must be ≥1; the migration is verified separately by re-reading the live input_schema rows and by schema_migrations carrying the 178 row.
4. The follow-up flip and the applyCTARecompute widening are intentionally OUT of this round; each returns to this gate with the delta-log evidence attached.
